The test image shows a close-up of a tomato fruit surface with multiple dark black spiky/hairy fungal structures (acervuli with setae) scattered across a reddish-orange surface, with white mycelium in the center. This is characteristic of Anthracnose (Colletotrichum), which produces acervuli with dark setae on fruit. The plant part is a pod/fruit.

Now I'll view one Anthracnose reference image.

The test image shows a macro close-up of tomato fruit with multiple black, spiky circular structures. These are Colletotrichum acervuli with dark setae (bristle-like spines) - the pathognomonic microscopic feature of Anthracnose. The white material in the center is mycelium/spore mass. The reddish fruit surface matches a tomato host.

The reference image confirms the macro-level anthracnose lesion pattern (sunken, darkened, concentric rings on fruit), while the test image zooms in to show the individual acervuli with setae, which are diagnostic for Colletotrichum/Anthracnose.

No other class in the list produces these spiny black acervuli on fruit surfaces.
